thread:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a 30% drop in token-latency samples on the NYC exporter cluster starting ~1768456700. Not a complete outage but large gaps in per-token buckets.
kevin: Hmm, did ingestion spike or exporter CPU starve? Any OTel queueing visible?
maria: Exporter host CPU looks fine, but export latency to metrics pipeline increased from ~30ms -> 500ms. Attached a small PromQL I ran: `sum by (route) (rate(redwood_token_latency_bucket[5m]))` — counts down across multiple routes.
taylor: Can you paste the exporter logs? Especially the flush intervals / backpressure logs from the StatsD->OTel adapter.
maria: log snippet: ```
2026-03-12T09:19:23Z WARN exporter: flush delayed=470ms queued=1200
2026-03-12T09:19:24Z INFO  exporter: dropped=0 retry_queue=0
2026-03-12T09:19:25Z WARN exporter: flush delayed=520ms queued=1180
```
kevin: Interesting — queued=1200 then 1180 (not monotonic), looks like periodic GC or latency spikes causing batches to be clipped. Could be the kernel selection heuristics on runtime side producing high-burst request patterns that the exporter doesn't handle.
metrics-bot: @channel Alert: high_export_latency detected on metrics-exporter-nyc (avg p95=520ms) — threshold 200ms exceeded.
infra-ops: I'm going to instrument token-level emit paths to add a per-request tag for kernel_variant and kv_hit (0/1). That should help correlate which model/kernel combos generate the gaps.
maria: Yes please. Also propose we run a short profiler on the exporter process to check syscalls around flush. Use `perf top` and capture samples for ~30s.
kevin: Meanwhile we should backfill missing histograms into the dashboards once we unblock ingestion. I suggest a two-step plan: 1) short-term backfill from raw traces stored in s3 (they contain token timestamps) 2) long-term job to reconstruct per-route token histograms from the trace replayer. Anyone object?
taylor: No objection. For step 1 I can produce a Spark job to parse traces -> StatsD-formatted counters and write to a backfill queue. Need a safe window: only touch 1768456600..1768456800 to avoid dupes.
maria: Perfect. Add guard flag `--dry-run` first. Also add a small dedupe key (trace_id:bucket:route) so we don't double-insert.
kevin: On infra side we'll bump exporter retry policy to increase buffer limit and enable `batch_endpoint: true` to reduce flush frequency by increasing batch_size. Quick config snippet to apply: ```yaml
exporter:
  batch_size: 5000
  max_buffer: 20000
  flush_interval_ms: 1000
  backoff: 200ms
```
metrics-bot: Change request posted to infra-config with id cfg-2026-03-12-17. Please review.
infra-ops: Also planning a canary deploy of the patched exporter to `nyc-canary` (2 nodes) before rolling. Timeline: canary in 30m, observe 1h, then full roll in 2h if stable.
taylor: For the dashboard backfill: I'll add a new per-route KPI `token_latency_p90_by_kernel` and populate with reprocessed data. Will coordinate with Observability to mark the period as "estimated" in the UI.
maria: After canary I'll run a targeted profiler on the runtime to see if kernel selection/kv cache thrashing correlates with the export bursts. If we confirm kv misses spike, we can enable prefix-KV caching window extension as a mitigation.
kevin: Assigning actions: infra-ops -> patch + canary; taylor -> backfill job + dry run; maria -> runtime profiling + correlation dashboards. Check-in in this thread after canary health metrics. :thumbsup:
